title: Fine-Tuning LLMs
subtitle: When and how to fine-tune vs prompt engineer

content.text: Fine-tuning trains the model on your data to specialise its behaviour. It is expensive and usually unnecessary — good prompting covers 90% of use cases.

content.code:
# Fine-tuning is typically done through provider APIs
# Example: OpenAI fine-tuning workflow
from openai import OpenAI
client = OpenAI()

# 1. Upload training data (JSONL format)
response = client.files.create(
    file=open("training_data.jsonl", "rb"),
    purpose="fine-tune"
)
file_id = response.id

# 2. Create a fine-tuning job
job = client.fine_tuning.jobs.create(
    training_file=file_id,
    model="gpt-4o-mini"
)

# 3. Wait and use the fine-tuned model
# client.chat.completions.create(model=job.fine_tuned_model, ...)

content.text: Always try prompt engineering + few-shot examples before fine-tuning. Fine-tuning costs money and time.

questions.question: When is fine-tuning most justified?
options: When you want to chat with an LLM
When you need consistent output formatting at scale and prompting has reached its limits
When you want to give an LLM new knowledge
Whenever you have more than 100 examples
questions.explanation: Fine-tuning is best for ingraining a specific style or format when prompting is inconsistent at high volumes.

faq.a: Anthropic offers fine-tuning for select enterprise customers. For most developers, prompt engineering with the base model is the recommended path.
